name: SITE Santa Fe
funding: No funder list is published. Its Business Council lists local galleries, hotels, distilleries and Century Bank. FY2024 revenue was $6.5M, with $4.2M in contributions.
watch: Board includes Louisa Stude Sarofim and Carl Thoma. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found, but no funder list exists to test.
records_note: It names 15 trustees and 10 advisers, benefit sponsors by tier for July 2026 and 31 Business Council firms; ProPublica holds Form 990s to 2024.

name: Skowhegan School of Painting & Sculpture
funding: About US$4.1M in expenses in 2023 (Form 990), all privately raised: a US$21M+ 75th-anniversary campaign that ended in Feb 2023, an annual gala and foundations.
watch: Summer residency in Maine. Campaign donors include the Kellen, Acquavella, Palm, Pollock-Krasner and Frankenthaler foundations and Agnes Gund.
records_note: Only the 2025 annual report is online, with donors named by giving level; Form 990s are on ProPublica and trustees and governors are listed.

name: Slought
funding: University of Pennsylvania cultural partnerships, Pennsylvania Council on the Arts, philanthropic grants; 501(c)(3) non-profit.
watch: Non-profit cultural organization on UPenn campus; archives of socio-political speech, psychoanalysis, and poetic resistance.

name: Smack Mellon
funding: NYSCA, NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, Andy Warhol Foundation, National Endowment for the Arts; 501(c)(3) non-profit.
watch: 501(c)(3) non-profit in DUMBO that supports women, queer and underrepresented artists through large industrial-scale commissions.

name: Smena Centre for Contemporary Culture
watch: Bookshop, gallery and festival; integrated the Bulat Galeev 'Prometheus' foundation in 2023; co-produces a 2026 show with Zarya in Vladivostok.
records_note: No official website for Smena could be found, so none of the four could be checked; press says it has no annual budget.

name: Solomon Islands National Museum
funding: A small government museum under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. In 2024 its virtual museum was funded by Australia's Digital Pasifik project with UK support.
watch: Founded in 1969 and a government institution since 1972. It went online in Oct 2024 with help from the New Zealand and Australian national libraries.
records_note: The museum has no site of its own and its government portal pages returned errors, so its reports, accounts, funders and board are unchecked.

name: Somerset House
funding: Trusts include AKO, Garfield Weston, Rothschild, Linbury and the National Lottery Heritage Fund. Corporate partners: Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, American Express, Virgin Atlantic Holidays, HSBC UK and Bloomberg.
watch: The ASA banned two HSBC climate adverts in October 2022. 260 UK artists asked London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026; neither targeted here.
records_note: Annual reports with financial statements from 2014-15 to 2023-24 on its site, an undated named supporters page, and trustees listed.

name: Sonic Acts
funding: Mondriaan Fund, Performing Arts Fund NL (Fonds Podiumkunsten), AFK, Creative Europe; non-profit foundation.
watch: Non-profit foundation and international research platform on the climate crisis, sound art and earth politics.

name: South London Gallery
funding: Ongoing support from Arts Council England, Southwark Council, Bukhman Foundation, Bloomberg Philanthropies and Garfield Weston Foundation. Corporate partners include Artsy and Bloomberg; galleries and patrons also give.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies funds it; 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026. SLG returned a Sackler gift in 2018.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the current supporters page names funders undated, and the trustees are listed.

name: Southern Exposure (SoEx)
funding: National Endowment for the Arts, Andy Warhol Foundation, San Francisco Arts Commission (SFAC); 501(c)(3) non-profit.
watch: Artist-centered non-profit in the Mission District since 1974, supporting visual artists.

name: Stacion - Center for Contemporary Art Prishtina
funding: Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports Kosovo, European Cultural Foundation, ERSTE Foundation; independent NGO.

name: The State Hermitage Museum
funding: Federal budget of the Russian Federation and state corporate sponsorships (VTB Bank, Gazprom).
watch: Director Mikhail Piotrovsky explicitly weaponized museum diplomacy as 'cultural operations' in support of state military aggression.
